diagnostic_focus.general_medicine: integrating broad multisystem clues and deciding which medical differential deserves priority
diagnostic_focus.internal_medicine: integrating unresolved multisystem findings and prioritizing the next medical diagnostic branch
diagnostic_focus.neurology: localizing neurologic dysfunction and separating central, peripheral, and neuromuscular causes
diagnostic_focus.surgery: deciding whether the pattern is primarily a surgical process and which surgical differential is most urgent
diagnostic_focus.cardiology: distinguishing cardiac ischemic, rhythm, and structural causes from non-cardiac mimics
diagnostic_focus.pulmonology: separating airway, parenchymal, pleural, and pulmonary vascular causes of respiratory symptoms
diagnostic_focus.gastroenterology: sorting hepatobiliary, pancreatic, luminal GI, and bleeding-related differentials
diagnostic_focus.nephrology: sorting intrinsic renal, post-renal, electrolyte, and inflammatory kidney processes
diagnostic_focus.infectious_disease: judging whether infection is the main driver and which infectious source best fits the evidence
diagnostic_focus.orthopedics: distinguishing fracture, joint, tendon, and mechanical musculoskeletal causes
diagnostic_focus.obstetrics_gynecology: sorting pregnancy-related, uterine, ovarian, and gynecologic urgent differentials
diagnostic_focus.urology: distinguishing obstructive, infectious, stone-related, and testicular/urinary tract causes
diagnostic_focus.psychiatry: separating primary psychiatric presentations from medical or neurologic mimics

next_steps.general_medicine: reconcile the ER data and decide the most informative next medical diagnostic step
next_steps.internal_medicine: review ER evidence, refine the differential, and recommend focused follow-up testing
next_steps.neurology: use neurologic pattern recognition to narrow the differential and identify confirmatory testing
next_steps.surgery: decide whether surgical pathology remains the leading explanation and what finding would confirm it
next_steps.cardiology: judge whether the pattern supports a cardiac diagnosis strongly enough for focused confirmation
next_steps.pulmonology: decide which respiratory diagnosis is best supported and what objective finding matters most
next_steps.gastroenterology: narrow the GI differential and identify the most discriminating objective clue
next_steps.nephrology: determine whether renal involvement is primary and which laboratory or urine clue is decisive
next_steps.infectious_disease: judge whether infection remains the lead diagnosis after reviewing objective data
next_steps.orthopedics: clarify whether the presentation is best explained by structural musculoskeletal pathology
next_steps.obstetrics_gynecology: determine whether the leading diagnosis is gynecologic or pregnancy-related
next_steps.urology: clarify whether the leading diagnosis is urinary tract, obstructive, or testicular in origin
next_steps.psychiatry: determine whether psychiatric framing is justified after reviewing current medical evidence

interview_questions.general_medicine: What symptom has changed the most since you first came to the ER?
interview_questions.internal_medicine: Have you noticed any other body system symptoms that seem connected to this problem?
interview_questions.neurology: Have the symptoms been fluctuating, and do they get worse with activity or better with rest?
interview_questions.surgery: Has the pain become more localized or more severe since it started?
interview_questions.cardiology: Have you noticed palpitations, exertional worsening, or chest pressure since arriving?
interview_questions.pulmonology: Has your breathing changed with exertion, lying down, or coughing?
interview_questions.gastroenterology: Have you had any vomiting, bleeding, or change in bowel movements since this began?
interview_questions.nephrology: Have you noticed any change in urine, swelling, rash, or recent medication exposure?
interview_questions.infectious_disease: Have you had any fevers, exposures, or new infectious symptoms since this started?
interview_questions.orthopedics: Does movement, weight bearing, or a specific position make the pain clearly worse?
interview_questions.obstetrics_gynecology: Have you had any bleeding, pelvic symptoms, or pregnancy-related concerns along with this?
interview_questions.urology: Have you had any urinary difficulty, blood in the urine, or flank-to-groin pain?
interview_questions.psychiatry: Have stress, mood changes, or similar prior episodes contributed to how this feels now?
